code: # Self-contained toy: two adjacent square polities. Only "P1" reports a # value in 1900, so when the series is rebuilt onto the boundaries active in # `ref_year` 2000 (both polities), "P2" is imputed from "P1"'s intensity. # `sf` is a suggested dependency, so the example runs only when it is there. if (requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)) {   make_square <- function(xmin, ymin, side) {     sf::st_polygon(list(rbind(       c(xmin, ymin),       c(xmin + side, ymin),       c(xmin + side, ymin + side),       c(xmin, ymin + side),       c(xmin, ymin)     )))   }   polities <- sf::st_sf(     polity_code = c("P1", "P2"),     start_year = c(1800L, 1800L),     end_year = c(2025L, 2025L),     geometry = sf::st_sfc(       make_square(0, 0, 2),       make_square(2, 0, 2),       crs = 4326     )   )   reported <- tibble::tibble(     year = 1900L,     polity_code = "P1",     value = 100   )   build_constant_territory_series(     reported,     ref_year = 2000,     polities = polities,     resolution = 50000,     verbose = FALSE   ) } #> # A tibble: 2 × 8 #>   target_polity_code  year value covered imputed imputed_share n_sources #>   <chr>              <int> <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>         <dbl>     <int> #> 1 P1                  1900   100     100       0             0         1 #> 2 P2                  1900   100       0     100             1         1 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: unallocated <dbl>

text: Convert FAOSTAT harvested area per-crop physical cropland using CROPGRIDS, return land extension keyed (year, area_code, item_cbs_code) FABIO footprint model. CROPGRIDS (Tang et al. 2024) reports, per crop country, harvested area crop (physical) area 2020. ratio genuinely per-crop multi-cropping correction — e.g. rice ~0.81 (heavily double-cropped), crops ~0.95-1.0 (single-cropped) — single country-level cropping-intensity factor, cell-level apportionment harvested share, reproduce. function applies per-(area, item) physical / harvested ratio WHEP harvested area year: \(physical = harvested \times (physical_{cg} / harvested_{cg})\). title: Build gridded landuse dataset — build_gridded_landuse
text: Disaggregate country-level FAOSTAT crop harvested areas 0.5-degree grid. reproduces core spatialization workflow LandInG toolbox, adapted WHEP conventions tidy data structures. algorithm follows three main steps: crop's country total distributed grid cells proportionally spatial reference pattern (e.g. Monfreda) weighted gridded cropland extent (e.g. LUH2/HYDE). total allocated harvested area cell exceeds capacity (cropland times multi-cropping suitability), excess iteratively redistributed using logit-based transformation. Individual crops aggregated crop functional types (CFTs).

title: Build gridded livestock dataset — build_gridded_livestock
text: Disaggregate country-level FAOSTAT livestock stocks emissions 0.5-degree grid. species group uses tailored spatial proxy: Ruminants (cattle, buffalo, sheep/goats, equines): LUH2 managed pasture (pastr) plus rangeland (range), optionally weighted static manure-intensity reference (West et al. 2014). Confined animals (pigs, poultry): LUH2 aggregate cropland, reflecting intensive farming co-location crop production. Range specialists (camels): LUH2 rangeland . Mixed (animals): 50/50 blend pasture cropland. country, year, species group function distributes national total proportionally cell-level proxy weights: $$\text{cell} = \frac{w_i}{\sum_{j \\text{country}} w_j}       \times T_{\text{country}}$$ \(w_i\) proxy weight cell \(\) (land-use hectares times optional reference-pattern intensity) \(T\) country total (heads emissions).

title: Build the livestock greenhouse-gas emissions extension. — build_livestock_ghg_extension
text: Aggregate per-animal IPCC livestock emissions footprint extension keyed (year, area_code, item_cbs_code), expressed kilograms carbon-dioxide equivalent (CO2e). bridges cohort-level emissions pipeline (calculate_livestock_emissions()) input-output grain used build_io_model() compute_footprint(), exactly like build_grassland_land_extension() land. Live-animal head counts come get_primary_production(), bridged IPCC species prepare_livestock_emissions(), resulting enteric manure emissions converted CO2e summed back live-animal commodity sector (item_cbs_code, e.g. 961 non-dairy cattle), sector build_io_model(). Two IPCC tiers available, selected tier: 1 (default): Tier 1 regional emission factors (IPCC 2019). needs species, country head counts, complete every country get_primary_production(). covers enteric manure methane manure N2O (direct indirect, default per-head nitrogen excretion rates). 2: Tier 2 cohort energy balance (IPCC 2019). derives enteric CH4 manure N2O per-animal energy nitrogen balance, finer resolution, requires cohort weight diet inputs. Animals whose emissions resolved (missing diet energy data) dropped warning rather entering footprint NA. per-head enteric manure emissions now sit range Tier 1 regional factors. Tier 1 remains default complete every country get_primary_production(), whereas Tier 2 needs cohort diet inputs. CO2e conversion uses 100-year global warming potentials selected gwp: "ar6" (default): IPCC AR6 (2021) Table 7.15, biogenic CH4 = 27, N2O = 273. "ar5": IPCC AR5 (2013), CH4 = 28, N2O = 265 (climate-carbon feedback). "ar4": IPCC AR4 (2007), CH4 = 25, N2O = 298.

Default FALSE. historical_data Optional harmonized historical production rows add LUH2 historical extension. May data frame path parquet/csv file. "none" (default, current published behaviour) leaves unmatched; pre-1962 production back-cast build warns. title: Assemble soil carbon inputs per cell, crop and year. — build_soil_carbon_inputs
text: Builds carbon returned soil crop residues, crop roots, weeds applied manure, carbon-input layer soil-organic-carbon turnover models (calculate_soc_dynamics()) consume. Soil-returned residue carbon (residue net fraction removed feed, fuel burning), root carbon weed (spontaneous-grass) carbon come calculate_npp_carbon_nitrogen() (per polity, crop year); manure carbon comes build_livestock_nutrient_flows()'s applied stream. four component carbon masses converted megagrams carbon (1 tonne = 1 Mg), gridded cells proportion crop's harvested area, divided cell-crop area give Mg C per hectare per year. carbon-weighted humification fraction computed per cell-year residue_humification, weed carbon humified weed (spontaneous-grass) coefficient. "polity" resolution component carbon masses summed back (area_code, item_prod_code, year) per-hectare values humified fraction re-derived polity totals.

what: Build a gridded soil water balance from LPJmL hydrology. — build_water_balance
title: Build a gridded soil water balance from LPJmL hydrology. — build_water_balance
text: Combines LPJmL monthly hydrology outputs annual per-cell water balance closes water_input_mm = aet_mm + runoff_mm + drainage_mm + soil_water_change_mm. Actual evapotranspiration (aet_mm) sum transpiration, evaporation interception components (LPJmL direct AET, PET temperature output). Water input precipitation plus irrigation. drainage_mm LPJmL deep seepage, leaching driver downstream; runoff_mm LPJmL total runoff (surface plus lateral), leaves cell laterally leaching term must appear budget. Drainage defaults native seepage; "residual" method instead reconstructs seepage water_input - aet - runoff - soil_water_change, use seepage file absent (equals seepage balance closes). Evapotranspiration split blue (irrigation-sourced) green (rain-sourced) part. result returned per grid cell, aggregated polity totals resolution = "polity". output also exposes footprint-relevant terms folded budget: prec_mm (precipitation) irrig_mm (applied irrigation, gross blue-water volume), satisfy water_input_mm = prec_mm + irrig_mm; blue_consump_mm green_consump_mm, LPJmL-native consumptive blue green water (per-CFT cft_consump_water_b / cft_consump_water_g cubes supplied, summed bands bands selects, otherwise blue green AET); cft_nir_mm, net irrigation requirement (LPJmL cft_nir), net blue-water demand, summed cell level data$cft_nir supplied NA otherwise. Potential evapotranspiration (pet_mm) comes CRU climate forcing drives LPJmL run NA forcing wired (see data$pet); PET formula fabricated .

what: Between-country population-weighted Gini of per-capita food supply. — calculate_food_gini
title: Between-country population-weighted Gini of per-capita food supply. — calculate_food_gini
text: Reduces per-capita nourishment series per-year, -country, population-weighted Gini coefficient, diagnostic unequally per-capita supply shared across countries (rescale per-country nourishment score). Within year, countries sorted descending per-capita supply; country's population fraction pop_frac share total supply mass value_frac (per-capita supply times population, world total) give score value_frac * (pop_frac + 2 * richer_frac), richer_frac cumulative population fraction strictly richer countries. Gini 1 - sum(score) countries year, 0 perfectly equal distribution rising toward 1 supply concentrates. Protein per-capita supply SJOS-N nourishment axis, default; passing different value_col (example energy_kcal_cap_day) takes Gini axis instead. Rows missing supply population value dropped computation.

title: Calculate LMDI decomposition. — calculate_lmdi
text: LMDI method decomposes changes target variable contributions multiple factors using logarithmic mean weights. implementation supports: Flexible identity specification: Automatic factor detection identity string. Support ratio calculations (implicit division). Sectoral aggregation [] notation. Sectoral grouping {} notation. Period analysis: function can decompose changes single multiple periods. Periods defined consecutive pairs periods vector. Grouping capabilities: Use .perform separate decompositions different groups (e.g., countries, regions) maintaining consistent factor structure.

title: Calculate LMDI decomposition. — calculate_lmdi
text: identity parameter uses special syntax define decomposition: Basic format: "target:factor1*factor2*factor3" Simple decomposition (sectors): Basic: "emissions:gdp*(emissions/gdp)" Complete: "emissions:(emissions/gdp)*(gdp/population)*population" Understanding bracket notation: Square brackets [] specify variables sum across categories, enabling structural decomposition. bracket aggregates values calculating ratios. Single-level structural decomposition: "emissions:activity*(activity[sector]/activity)*(emissions[sector]/activity[sector])" Creates 3 factors: Activity level, Sectoral structure, Sectoral intensity. Multi-level structural decomposition: Two levels: "emissions:activity*(activity[sector]/activity)*(activity[sector+fuel]/activity[sector])*(emissions[sector+fuel]/activity[sector+fuel])" Creates 4 factors: Activity level, Sector structure, Fuel structure, Sectoral-fuel intensity.

title: Calculate LMDI decomposition. — calculate_lmdi
code: # In these examples, 'activity' is a measure of scale # (e.g., GDP in million USD) and 'intensity' is the target # variable per unit activity (e.g., emissions per million USD). # The units are illustrative; adapt to your context. # --- Shared sample data --- data_simple <- tibble::tribble(   ~year, ~activity, ~intensity, ~emissions,   2010,  1000,      0.10,       100,   2011,  1100,      0.12,       132,   2012,  1200,      0.09,       108,   2013,  1300,      0.10,       130 )  # --- 1. Year-over-year decomposition (default) --- # Decompose annual emission changes into activity and intensity effects. # The additive column sums to the total change in emissions each period. calculate_lmdi(   data_simple,   identity = "emissions:activity*intensity",   time_var = year,   verbose = FALSE ) |>   dplyr::select(     period,     component_type,     factor_label,     additive,     multiplicative   ) #> # A tibble: 9 × 5 #>   period    component_type factor_label additive multiplicative #>   <chr>     <chr>          <chr>           <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1 2010-2011 factor         activity        11.0           1.1   #> 2 2010-2011 factor         intensity       21.0           1.2   #> 3 2010-2011 target         emissions       32             1.32  #> 4 2011-2012 factor         activity        10.4           1.09  #> 5 2011-2012 factor         intensity      -34.4           0.75  #> 6 2011-2012 target         emissions      -24             0.818 #> 7 2012-2013 factor         activity         9.50          1.08  #> 8 2012-2013 factor         intensity       12.5           1.11  #> 9 2012-2013 target         emissions       22             1.20   # --- 2. Single baseline-to-end period --- # Pass a two-element periods vector to get a single cumulative period # instead of year-over-year results. calculate_lmdi(   data_simple,   identity = "emissions:activity*intensity",   time_var = year,   periods = c(2010, 2013),   verbose = FALSE ) |>   dplyr::select(     period,     component_type,     factor_label,     additive,     multiplicative   ) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   period    component_type factor_label additive multiplicative #>   <chr>     <chr>          <chr>           <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1 2010-2013 factor         activity           30            1.3 #> 2 2010-2013 factor         intensity           0            1   #> 3 2010-2013 target         emissions          30            1.3  # --- 3. Year-over-year AND one cumulative summary period --- # Use periods_2 to append an extra comparison period alongside the # year-over-year results. calculate_lmdi(   data_simple,   identity = "emissions:activity*intensity",   time_var = year,   periods = c(2010, 2011, 2012, 2013),   periods_2 = c(2010, 2013),   verbose = FALSE ) |>   dplyr::select(     period,     component_type,     factor_label,     additive,     multiplicative   ) #> # A tibble: 12 × 5 #>    period    component_type factor_label additive multiplicative #>    <chr>     <chr>          <chr>           <dbl>          <dbl> #>  1 2010-2011 factor         activity        11.0           1.1   #>  2 2010-2011 factor         intensity       21.0           1.2   #>  3 2010-2011 target         emissions       32             1.32  #>  4 2011-2012 factor         activity        10.4           1.09  #>  5 2011-2012 factor         intensity      -34.4           0.75  #>  6 2011-2012 target         emissions      -24             0.818 #>  7 2012-2013 factor         activity         9.50          1.08  #>  8 2012-2013 factor         intensity       12.5           1.11  #>  9 2012-2013 target         emissions       22             1.20  #> 10 2010-2013 factor         activity        30             1.3   #> 11 2010-2013 factor         intensity        0             1     #> 12 2010-2013 target         emissions       30             1.3    # --- 4. Per-country decomposition with .by --- # Separate LMDI runs per country; results are stacked with a country column. data_countries <- tibble::tribble(   ~year, ~country, ~activity, ~intensity, ~emissions,   2010, "ESP", 1000, 0.10, 100,   2011, "ESP", 1100, 0.11, 121,   2012, "ESP", 1200, 0.10, 120,   2010, "FRA", 2000, 0.05, 100,   2011, "FRA", 2200, 0.05, 110,   2012, "FRA", 2400, 0.05, 120 )  calculate_lmdi(   data_countries,   identity = "emissions:activity*intensity",   time_var = year,   .by = "country",   verbose = FALSE ) |>   dplyr::select(     country,     period,     component_type,     factor_label,     additive,     multiplicative   ) #> # A tibble: 12 × 6 #>    country period    component_type factor_label additive multiplicative #>    <chr>   <chr>     <chr>          <chr>           <dbl>          <dbl> #>  1 ESP     2010-2011 factor         activity         10.5          1.1   #>  2 ESP     2010-2011 factor         intensity        10.5          1.1   #>  3 ESP     2010-2011 target         emissions        21            1.21  #>  4 ESP     2011-2012 factor         activity         10.5          1.09  #>  5 ESP     2011-2012 factor         intensity       -11.5          0.909 #>  6 ESP     2011-2012 target         emissions        -1            0.992 #>  7 FRA     2010-2011 factor         activity         10            1.1   #>  8 FRA     2010-2011 factor         intensity         0            1     #>  9 FRA     2010-2011 target         emissions        10            1.1   #> 10 FRA     2011-2012 factor         activity         10            1.09  #> 11 FRA     2011-2012 factor         intensity         0            1     #> 12 FRA     2011-2012 target         emissions        10            1.09   # --- 5. Ratio notation --- # Express factors as explicit ratios (e.g. intensity = emissions/activity). # Factor labels in the output preserve the ratio form for clarity. calculate_lmdi(   data_simple,   identity = "emissions:(emissions/activity)*activity",   time_var = year,   verbose = FALSE ) |>   dplyr::select(     period,     component_type,     factor_label,     additive,     multiplicative   ) #> # A tibble: 9 × 5 #>   period    component_type factor_label       additive multiplicative #>   <chr>     <chr>          <chr>                 <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1 2010-2011 factor         emissions/activity    21.0           1.20  #> 2 2010-2011 factor         activity              11.0           1.1   #> 3 2010-2011 target         emissions             32             1.32  #> 4 2011-2012 factor         emissions/activity   -34.4           0.750 #> 5 2011-2012 factor         activity              10.4           1.09  #> 6 2011-2012 target         emissions            -24             0.818 #> 7 2012-2013 factor         emissions/activity    12.5           1.11  #> 8 2012-2013 factor         activity               9.50          1.08  #> 9 2012-2013 target         emissions             22.0           1.20   # --- 6. Structural (sectoral) decomposition with [] notation --- # Decomposes emissions into: #   total_activity * sector_structure * sector_intensity # [] sums the bracketed variable across sector before forming ratios, # enabling proper structural decomposition. data_sectors <- tibble::tribble(   ~year, ~sector, ~activity, ~emissions,   2010, "industry", 600, 60,   2010, "transport", 400, 40,   2011, "industry", 700, 63,   2011, "transport", 500, 55 ) |>   dplyr::group_by(year) |>   dplyr::mutate(total_activity = sum(activity)) |>   dplyr::ungroup()  calculate_lmdi(   data_sectors,   identity = paste0(     "emissions:",     "total_activity*",     "(activity[sector]/total_activity)*",     "(emissions[sector]/activity[sector])"   ),   time_var = year,   verbose = FALSE ) |>   dplyr::select(     period,     component_type,     factor_label,     additive,     multiplicative   ) #> # A tibble: 4 × 5 #>   period    component_type factor_label                  additive multiplicative #>   <chr>     <chr>          <chr>                            <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1 2010-2011 factor         total_activity                  19.8            1.20  #> 2 2010-2011 factor         activity[sector]/total_activ…    0.191          1.00  #> 3 2010-2011 factor         emissions[sector]/activity[s…   -1.99           0.982 #> 4 2010-2011 target         emissions                       18              1.18   # --- 7. Custom factor labels --- # Replace raw variable names with readable labels for reporting. # Supply one label per term (target first, then each factor in order). calculate_lmdi(   data_simple,   identity = "emissions:activity*intensity",   identity_labels = c(     "Total Emissions",     "Activity Effect",     "Intensity Effect"   ),   time_var = year,   verbose = FALSE ) |>   dplyr::select(     period,     component_type,     factor_label,     additive,     multiplicative   ) #> # A tibble: 9 × 5 #>   period    component_type factor_label     additive multiplicative #>   <chr>     <chr>          <chr>               <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1 2010-2011 factor         Activity Effect     11.0           1.1   #> 2 2010-2011 factor         Intensity Effect    21.0           1.2   #> 3 2010-2011 target         Total Emissions     32             1.32  #> 4 2011-2012 factor         Activity Effect     10.4           1.09  #> 5 2011-2012 factor         Intensity Effect   -34.4           0.75  #> 6 2011-2012 target         Total Emissions    -24             0.818 #> 7 2012-2013 factor         Activity Effect      9.50          1.08  #> 8 2012-2013 factor         Intensity Effect    12.5           1.11  #> 9 2012-2013 target         Total Emissions     22             1.20   # --- 8. Rolling mean smoothing before decomposition --- # A 3-year rolling mean reduces noise in volatile series before # computing LMDI weights. Edge years use partial windows (fewer # than k observations) so no periods are lost. data_smooth <- tibble::tibble(   year      = 2010:2020,   activity  = seq(1000, 2000, length.out = 11),   intensity = rep(0.1, 11),   emissions = seq(1000, 2000, length.out = 11) * 0.1 )  calculate_lmdi(   data_smooth,   identity = "emissions:activity*intensity",   time_var = year,   rolling_mean = 3,   verbose = FALSE ) |>   dplyr::select(     period,     component_type,     factor_label,     additive,     multiplicative   ) #> # A tibble: 30 × 5 #>    period    component_type factor_label additive multiplicative #>    <chr>     <chr>          <chr>           <dbl>          <dbl> #>  1 2010-2011 factor         activity            5           1.05 #>  2 2010-2011 factor         intensity           0           1    #>  3 2010-2011 target         emissions           5           1.05 #>  4 2011-2012 factor         activity           10           1.09 #>  5 2011-2012 factor         intensity           0           1    #>  6 2011-2012 target         emissions          10           1.09 #>  7 2012-2013 factor         activity           10           1.08 #>  8 2012-2013 factor         intensity           0           1    #>  9 2012-2013 target         emissions          10           1.08 #> 10 2013-2014 factor         activity           10           1.08 #> # ℹ 20 more rows

title: Estimate ammonia-N volatilisation with the MANNER process-based model. — calculate_manner_nh3
text: Ports MANNER (Nicholson et al. 2013) process-based ammonia volatilisation model. Dispatches fertiliser one two independent paths: synthetic-fertiliser path ("Urea", "", "CAN", "") driven soil pH, application rate, rainfall temperature, organic-manure path ("cattle_slurry", "pig_slurry", "FYM", "poultry_manure", "urban") driven rainfall, temperature, wind speed, application technique, system (arable/grassland) incorporation delay.

title: Estimate ammonia-N volatilisation with the MANNER process-based model. — calculate_manner_nh3
text: n_applied_t Numeric, nitrogen applied (t). fertiliser One "Urea", "", "CAN", "" (synthetic path) "cattle_slurry", "pig_slurry", "FYM", "poultry_manure", "urban" (organic path). drivers named list driver values. Synthetic path: soil_ph (numeric soil pH), rate_kg_ha (numeric N application rate, kg N/ha), rainfall_mm (numeric period precipitation, mm), irrigated (logical), temp_c (numeric application-period temperature, deg C), temp_c_annual_mean (numeric annual mean temperature, deg C; used CAN/). Organic path: rainfall_mm, irrigated, windspeed_ms (numeric wind speed, m/s), technique (one six manner_params technique keys), system ("Arable" "Grassland"), temp_c, incorporation_delay_h (numeric hours surface application soil incorporation, Inf/NA incorporation), species (optional; one eight manure_inorganic_n species, used look inorganic_n_fraction; omitted falls back manure type's default species, ignored entirely "urban"). example TRUE, return small fixture instead computing drivers. Defaults FALSE.

"urban" bypasses lookup entirely: fixes inorganic_n_fraction = 0.5 regardless species, matching nh3.r:102-104. text: Two methods partitioning nitrogen surplus leached nitrate topsoil-denitrified nitrogen. "meisinger_drainage" (default, n_fun.r:932-988) full Spain_Hist cascade: bins annual drainage soil organic matter share, looks topsoil denitrification share meisinger_denitrification, applies subsoil NO3 reduction (subsoil_no3_reduction) carbon--nitrogen leaching attenuation, re-derives denitrification_n_t residual n_surplus_t minus computed no3_n_t (raw denitrification share intermediate; see Details). what: Estimate direct soil N2O emissions from applied nitrogen. — calculate_soil_n2o
title: Estimate direct soil N2O emissions from applied nitrogen. — calculate_soil_n2o
text: Three emission-factor regimes direct nitrous oxide nitrogen applied soil. "ipcc2019" (default) IPCC 2019 Tier 1 climate-disaggregated EF1, needing climate: reuses n2o_efs_disaggregated table's two climate-level rows (irrig_type == "Tier_1" ATL, irrig_type == "Med_average" MED, 0.010 wet / 0.005 dry) mf multiplier; ATL value (0.010) value documented EF1 build_crop_soil_n2o_extension(), pulled one shared source truth rather hardcoded second time. default internationally standard, globally applicable Tier 1 method. "aguilera" (n_fun.r:906-912) finer Mediterranean-calibrated disaggregation (Cayuela et al. 2017), selectable irrig_type/fert_type granularity available regional emission factors apply: n2o_direct_n_t = n_input_t * ef * mf, ef n2o_efs_disaggregated (irrig_type, climate), mf fertiliser_n2o_modifiers (fert_type, climate). "ipcc2006" uses n2o_efs_ipcc2006 table (IPCC 2006 Tier 1 defaults, flat 0.010 except flooded rice 0.003), keyed like "aguilera" (irrig_type, climate) mf multiplier.

what: Check footprint conservation against direct extensions. — check_footprint_conservation
title: Check footprint conservation against direct extensions. — check_footprint_conservation
text: Verify master input-output accounting identity footprint: environmental pressure embodied across final demand traced back origin sector equal direct extension (source pressure) sector. footprint engine zeroes negative coefficients, caps column sums, drops near-zero-output sectors (FABIO conventions), identity holds approximately. check quantifies discrepancy per origin sector instead asserting exact equality. Crucially detects -tracing (pressure silently disappears never reaches final demand), compute_footprint()'s conserve_extensions bounding never reports rescales results downward. positive side extensions traced, matching engine, traces pmax(extensions, 0) ignores sectors output <= output_tol.

title: Check footprint conservation against direct extensions. — check_footprint_conservation
code: check_footprint_conservation(   footprint,   extensions,   labels,   x_vec,   output_tol = 1e-08,   tol = 0.01 )

title: Check footprint conservation against direct extensions. — check_footprint_conservation
text: footprint Footprint tibble compute_footprint(), origin_area, origin_item value columns. extensions Numeric vector environmental extensions per sector, passed compute_footprint(). labels Tibble area_code item_cbs_code mapping sector meaning, passed compute_footprint(). x_vec Numeric vector total output per sector. output_tol Minimum output sector traceable. Sectors x_vec <= output_tol contribute zero direct pressure, matching compute_footprint(). tol Relative tolerance conservation status. Discrepancies within tol direct pressure "ok".

title: Check footprint conservation against direct extensions. — check_footprint_conservation
text: tibble one row per origin sector: origin_area: Country pressure occurs. origin_item: Item causing pressure. direct: Direct (source) extension sector. embodied: Footprint traced back sector. discrepancy: embodied - direct. rel_discrepancy: discrepancy / direct (NA direct zero). status: One "ok", "under_traced", "dropped" (embodied zero direct positive) "over_traced". Rows ordered descending absolute relative discrepancy.

title: Check footprint conservation against direct extensions. — check_footprint_conservation
code: z_mat <- matrix(c(0, 5, 10, 0), nrow = 2) x_vec <- c(100, 200) y_mat <- matrix(c(85, 195), ncol = 1) extensions <- c(50, 30) labels <- tibble::tibble(   area_code = c(1L, 1L),   item_cbs_code = c(1L, 2L) ) fp <- compute_footprint(   x_vec = x_vec, y_mat = y_mat, extensions = extensions,   labels = labels, z_mat = z_mat ) #> ℹ Computing footprint for 2 sectors. #>   2 sectors have non-zero extensions. #>   Final demand: 1 column. #> Sparse solve path (no dense Leontief inverse). #> Computing footprints... #> ✔ Footprint complete: 2 non-zero flows. check_footprint_conservation(fp, extensions, labels, x_vec) #> # A tibble: 2 × 7 #>   origin_area origin_item direct embodied discrepancy rel_discrepancy status     #>         <int>       <int>  <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>           <dbl> <chr>      #> 1           1           1     50     47.5     -2.51          -0.0501  under_tra… #> 2           1           2     30     30.0     -0.0376        -0.00125 ok

text: Trace environmental extensions supply chain using Leontief inverse, following FABIO methodology (Bruckner et al., 2019). footprint shows much environmental pressure (e.g. land use, water, emissions) embodied final consumption product country. multiplier matrix computed \(MP_{ij} = (e_i / X_i) \cdot L_{ij}\), \(e_i\) extension sector \(\). demand category, footprint decomposed per target item using FABIO diagonal approach: \(FP = MP \cdot \text{diag}(y)\), aggregated item. large systems, pass z_mat x_vec instead l_inv. solves \((- ) x = Y\) directly using sparse LU factorisation, avoiding dense Leontief inverse entirely reducing memory \(O(n^2)\) \(O(nnz)\). z_mat l_inv paths give identical results largest column sum stays 1 (Leontief inverse non-negative). 1 paths can diverge: dense inverse zeroes negative entries whereas sparse solve drops resulting negative embodied flows, precomputed l_inv may capped differently (compute_leontief_inverse() defaults conservative cap 1). z_mat path emits warning happens; max_column_sum ignored l_inv supplied directly.

title: Compute Leontief inverse. — compute_leontief_inverse
text: Compute Leontief inverse matrix intermediate flows total output. Leontief inverse captures direct indirect requirements across entire supply chain, enabling footprint tracing. technical coefficients matrix computed \(A_{ij} = Z_{ij} / X_j\), representing input sector \(\) needed per unit output sector \(j\). Column sums capped using max_column_sum avoid singular systems inconsistent supply-use data. default uses 1 - value_added_floor, preserving previous conservative behavior explicit Leontief inverses. Leontief inverse \(L = (- )^{-1}\). large systems (thousands sectors) function usable: dense L matrix requires \(n^2 \times 8\) bytes memory (e.g. ~4.8 GiB n = 25 000). Use compute_footprint() directly z_mat x_vec instead, solves \((- ) x = Y\) without ever materialising L. Accepts dense sparse (Matrix package) inputs.

One province of each of three categories: Lugo is dominated by # grassland N, Sevilla by synthetic N on herbaceous production, and Huelva # by synthetic N where the local production is woody (acorns). prod_destiny <- tibble::tribble(   ~year, ~province_name, ~box, ~item, ~origin, ~destiny, ~mg_n,   2000, "Lugo", "semi_natural_agroecosystems", "Grassland",   "semi_natural_agroecosystems", "livestock_rum", 900,   2000, "Sevilla", "semi_natural_agroecosystems", "Grassland",   "semi_natural_agroecosystems", "livestock_rum", 100,   2000, "Huelva", "semi_natural_agroecosystems", "Grassland",   "semi_natural_agroecosystems", "livestock_rum", 30,   2000, "Huelva", "semi_natural_agroecosystems", "Acorns",   "semi_natural_agroecosystems", "export", 200,   2000, "Lugo", "Cropland", "Maize and products",   "Outside", "livestock_mono", 20,   2000, "Sevilla", "Cropland", "Maize and products",   "Outside", "livestock_mono", 50,   2000, "Huelva", "Cropland", "Maize and products",   "Outside", "livestock_mono", 10 )  soil_inputs <- tibble::tribble(   ~year, ~province_name, ~synthetic,   2000, "Lugo", 10,   2000, "Sevilla", 400,   2000, "Huelva", 150 )  create_alfredos_typologies(   soil_inputs = soil_inputs,   prod_destiny = prod_destiny,   years = 2000 ) #> # A tibble: 3 × 9 #>    year province_name grass_N fertiliser_N feed_import_N woody herbaceous #>   <dbl> <chr>           <dbl>        <dbl>         <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl> #> 1  2000 Huelva             30          150            10   200         30 #> 2  2000 Lugo              900           10            20     0        900 #> 3  2000 Sevilla           100          400            50     0        100 #> # ℹ 2 more variables: woody_share <dbl>, Category <chr>

Simple categorical proxy (e.g., "region"): Auto-detects categorical columns interprets value_col:region. Aggregates value_col specified groups. Advanced syntax (e.g., "gdp:region"): Format "variable:group1+group2". Aggregates variable specified groups. Hierarchical fallback (e.g., c("population", "gdp:region")): Tries first proxy, falls back second first fails. Weighted aggregation (e.g., "gdp[population]"): Weight variable specified column aggregation. time_col column containing time values. Default: year. .character vector grouping variables (optional). max_gap Numeric. Maximum gap size fill using growth method. Default: Inf. max_gap_linear Numeric. Maximum gap size linear interpolation fallback. Default: 3. fill_scope Quosure. Filter expression limit filling scope. Default: NULL. value_smooth_window Integer. Window size centered moving average applied value column gap-filling. Useful variables high inter-annual variability. NULL (default), smoothing applied. proxy_smooth_window Integer. Window size moving average smoothing proxy reference values computing growth rates. Default: 1. output_format Character. Output format: "clean" "detailed". Default: "clean". verbose Logical. what: Assemble monthly SOC climate drivers from CRU climate and LPJmL hydrology. — get_soc_climate_drivers
title: Assemble monthly SOC climate drivers from CRU climate and LPJmL hydrology. — get_soc_climate_drivers
text: Builds monthly per-cell climate drivers soil-organic-carbon decomposition modifiers consume: air temperature, topsoil soil-water saturation, monthly precipitation potential evapotranspiration (Century modifier drivers), monthly water-minus-potential- evapotranspiration surplus (RothC/HSOC driver), annual water balance (AMG driver), volumetric soil water content field-capacity, wilting-point porosity references (ICBM moisture drivers) clay content. Air temperature comes CRU TS 4.09 (read_cru_climate() "tmp", degrees Celsius); potential evapotranspiration CRU "pet" (mm/day), converted monthly total multiplying days month; water input (precipitation plus irrigation) LPJmL run consistent hydrology produced soil water content; soil water content LPJmL directly (read_lpjml_hydrology() "swc", topmost layer). soil hydraulic references (field capacity, wilting point, porosity) come dominant HWSD texture class cell via read_soil_hydraulic(), volumetric soil water content theta = swc_topsoil * porosity (LPJmL fractional saturation scaled cell porosity). Clay content soil-texture covariate supplied via data$clay; polity key comes cell-polity crosswalk (data$cell_polity).

what: Harmonize advanced cases with interpolation for 1:N groups — harmonize_interpolate
title: Harmonize advanced cases with interpolation for 1:N groups — harmonize_interpolate
text: Harmonize data containing "simple" "1:n" mappings. "simple" covers 1:1 N:1 relationships (values summed). "1:n" groups (one original item splits several harmonized items) function computes value shares across full year range, interpolates missing shares, applies split values. Important 1:n mappings: original item splits multiple harmonized items (e.g., "wheatrice" "wheat" "rice"), provide one row per target item_code_harm. row item, year, value, differing item_code_harm. example, disaggregate "wheatrice": Row 1: item = "wheatrice", item_code_harm = 1 Row 2: item = "wheatrice", item_code_harm = 2 provide single row; function create duplicates automatically. 1:n contribution can turn unvaluable, value missing share neither computed interpolated (e.g. every year group zero total). contributions dropped warning rather summed, one missing value turn observed "simple" values (item_code, year) cell NA.

2001 is interpolated. df_years <- tibble::tribble(   ~item, ~item_code_harm, ~year, ~value, ~type,   "wheat", 1, 2000, 6, "simple",   "rice", 2, 2000, 4, "simple",   "wheatrice", 1, 2001, 10, "1:n",   "wheatrice", 2, 2001, 10, "1:n",   "wheat", 1, 2002, 8, "simple",   "rice", 2, 2002, 2, "simple" ) harmonize_interpolate(df_years) #> # A tibble: 6 × 3 #>   item_code  year value #>       <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1         1  2001     7 #> 2         2  2001     3 #> 3         1  2000     6 #> 4         2  2000     4 #> 5         1  2002     8 #> 6         2  2002     2  # With extra grouping columns df_grouped <- tibble::tribble(   ~item, ~item_code_harm, ~year, ~value, ~type, ~country,   "wheat", 1, 2000, 6, "simple", "usa",   "rice", 2, 2000, 4, "simple", "usa",   "wheatrice", 1, 2001, 10, "1:n", "usa",   "wheatrice", 2, 2001, 10, "1:n", "usa",   "wheat", 1, 2002, 8, "simple", "usa",   "rice", 2, 2002, 2, "simple", "usa",   "wheat", 1, 2002, 8, "simple", "germany" ) harmonize_interpolate(df_grouped, country) #> # A tibble: 7 × 4 #>   item_code  year country value #>       <dbl> <dbl> <chr>   <dbl> #> 1         1  2001 usa         7 #> 2         2  2001 usa         3 #> 3         1  2000 usa         6 #> 4         2  2000 usa         4 #> 5         1  2002 usa         8 #> 6         2  2002 usa         2 #> 7         1  2002 germany     8

title: Interpolate anchor points at arbitrary output positions. — interp_vec
text: Vector-level interpolation primitive: anchor positions values , one interpolated value per requested output position . log_space = TRUE output point filled log space (constant compound growth rate) whenever bracketing anchors finite strictly positive; every point falls back ordinary linear interpolation. rule, internal implementation, fill_linear() applies log_space = TRUE. fill_linear() data-frame gap filler needs target rows already exist; interp_vec() callers hold plain vectors need values positions pre-existing row, call primitive per gap segment inside guard logic.

title: Interpolate anchor points at arbitrary output positions. — interp_vec
text: x Numeric vector anchor positions, example years. need sorted. y Numeric vector anchor values, length x. xout Numeric vector positions interpolate . need sorted; results follow order xout. log_space Logical. TRUE, output point bracketed two finite strictly positive anchors interpolated log space (constant compound growth rate); point falls back linear interpolation. Default: FALSE, .e. linear interpolation everywhere. rule Either 1 2, passed stats::approx() handle output positions outside anchor range. 1 (default) returns NA , 2 carries nearest anchor value. Log space never applies outside anchor range.

Anchors whose value infinite kept, segment bounded one never eligible log space. fewer two usable anchors remain nothing interpolate , every element y method NA. output position coincides anchor position returns anchor's value unchanged, labelled "linear", nothing needed interpolating . particular log space never rebuilds anchor value handed, perturb last bits.

code: # Constant compound growth: the 2005 midpoint of 1 and 1024 is 32, whereas # linear interpolation returns the arithmetic midpoint 512.5. interp_vec(c(2000, 2010), c(1, 1024), xout = 2005, log_space = TRUE) #> $y #> [1] 32 #>  #> $method #> [1] "loglinear" #>  interp_vec(c(2000, 2010), c(1, 1024), xout = 2005) #> $y #> [1] 512.5 #>  #> $method #> [1] "linear" #>   # A non-positive anchor makes log space undefined, so the point stays linear. interp_vec(c(2000, 2010), c(0, 10), xout = 2005, log_space = TRUE) #> $y #> [1] 5 #>  #> $method #> [1] "linear" #>   # Several output positions at once, from an unsorted anchor set. With # `rule = 2` the position beyond the last anchor carries that anchor value. interp_vec(   x = c(2010, 2000, 2005),   y = c(400, 100, 200),   xout = c(2002, 2007, 2015),   log_space = TRUE,   rule = 2 ) #> $y #> [1] 131.9508 263.9016 400.0000 #>  #> $method #> [1] "loglinear" "loglinear" "linear"    #>
